name: Double Underhook Pass
summary: A double-underhook pass reaches beneath both thighs after the high rubber-guard clinch has opened, then clears the legs under controlled pressure.
description: A double-underhook pass reaches beneath both thighs after the high rubber-guard clinch has opened, then clears the legs under controlled pressure.
overview:
The top player faces a bottom guard player using Crackhead Control; the head, shoulder or arm may still be enclosed. Do not thread both arms beneath the legs while the head and shoulders remain trapped in Crackhead Control. A double-under pass is a new configuration after release.

Avoid extending an arm between the high legs where it can be isolated. A second leg climbing behind your head increases the posture-control problem. Keep a balanced base and early inside frames; tap instead of moving against a completed choke or joint lock.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Eddie Bravo — MTS 169: the Pump](https://www.10thplanetjj.com/techniques/mts-169-rubber-guard-the-pump/); [10th Planet Costa Mesa — basic path with double bagger](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W2OFKidf9lE).

flashcards.question: Double Underhook Pass (top): What must clear before reaching beneath both thighs?
flashcards.answer: The double-under passing setup begins after the head, shoulders and arms clear the high rubber-guard enclosure.
flashcards.answer_line: The high-leg trap around your head and shoulders

plausible: Only the opponent's ankles below your waist
Only your free wrist from their grip
trap: Only one lower knee from between your legs

flashcards.question: Double Underhook Pass (top): In the completed hip-clasp setup, where are both arms routed?
flashcards.answer: After opening guard and clearing the high clinch, place both arms beneath the thighs.

plausible: One above a thigh and one below
Outside both thighs

flashcards.question: Double Underhook Pass (top): Where do the hands clasp in the demonstrated leg-gathering setup?
flashcards.answer: The primary demonstration clasps near the hips and hugs the legs together.
flashcards.answer_line: Near the hips while hugging both thighs

plausible: Near the knees while the hips remain out of reach
Over the thighs while both elbows flare outward
trap: Around one thigh while the second stays free

flashcards.question: Double Underhook Pass (top): What supports the opponent's hips as you sit back and posture?
flashcards.answer: With the legs gathered, the demonstrated setup brings the opponent's hips onto the passer's thighs without using the neck as a fulcrum.
flashcards.answer_line: Your thighs beneath their raised hips

plausible: Your forearms beneath the backs of their knees
The mat beneath hips that have not been lifted
trap: Your hands beneath their lower calves

flashcards.question: Double Underhook Pass (top): What contact does the shown pass add while one hand supports the hips?
flashcards.answer: The demonstration retains hip support and uses the opposite shoulder to guide the passing direction.
flashcards.answer_line: A grip on the opposite shoulder

plausible: A grip on the near elbow only
A grip behind the head only
trap: A palm against the near ribs only

flashcards.question: Double Underhook Pass (top): What must clear before you settle a side pin?
flashcards.answer: After releasing high guard, complete the leg clearance before settling beside the torso.
flashcards.answer_line: Both knees and the remaining leg hooks

plausible: Only one thigh while the other knee stays inside
Only the head from the old high clinch
trap: Only the opponent's hand from your shoulder

flashcards.question: Double Underhook Pass (top): How does the starting high clinch differ from the pass setup?
flashcards.answer: Crackhead's high posture clinch must open before the arms can establish the distinct double-under configuration.
flashcards.answer_line: Your shoulders are still inside high legs

plausible: Your forearms already lie under both free thighs
Your head is free above legs crossed at the waist
trap: Your shoulders sit beyond both knees beside the chest

flashcards.question: Double Underhook Pass (top): Why maintain hip control as you circle past the knees?
flashcards.answer: Hip control keeps the legs together while the passer changes angle; it does not replace the need to clear them.
flashcards.answer_line: To gather the legs as you circle past them

plausible: To hold the hips without controlling leg separation
To keep your chest centered between both thighs
trap: To replace clearing the inside knee with hip pressure

flashcards.question: Double Underhook Pass (top): The partner's weight folds onto the neck; what should change?
flashcards.answer: Do not use the neck as a load-bearing pivot. Reduce pressure and re-establish controlled support or reset.
flashcards.answer_line: Unload and restore supported hip control

plausible: Keep driving forward while the hips lose support
Pull the knees farther beyond the head
trap: Maintain the same fold while moving around the knees

flashcards.question: Double Underhook Pass (top): When can chest and crossface pressure stabilize the result?
flashcards.answer: Use balanced chest contact and controlled shoulder pressure in the settled side pin after leg clearance.
flashcards.answer_line: After the knees clear and side contact is established

plausible: While the head remains inside the original high clinch
Before either thigh has been gathered
trap: As soon as one hand touches the far shoulder

defender.name: Double Underhook Pass Defender
defender.description: Double Underhook Pass (defender): Establish the first high leg and its hand support before adding the second leg. Reinforce the clinch without forcing the knees beyond a comfortable hip angle.
defender.overview:
The top player faces a bottom guard player using Crackhead Control; the head, shoulder or arm may still be enclosed. Do not thread both arms beneath the legs while the head and shoulders remain trapped in Crackhead Control. A double-under pass is a new configuration after release.

Establish the first high leg and its hand support before adding the second leg. Reinforce the clinch without forcing the knees beyond a comfortable hip angle. Do not assume that high legs alone have isolated an arm or completed Dead Orchard.

Use hip position and connected leg pressure rather than pulling the feet against fixed knees. Lower the reinforcing leg while preserving the first shin connection if you need Mission Control again. Release and frame when the opponent compresses your upper back or you cannot comfortably maintain the clinch.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Make the early escape by framing against the shoulders and using hip movement to recover a knee before the passer closes both underhooks. After the legs are lifted together, reset rather than trying to wrench a knee sideways against the fixed grips.
key_principles: Start with broken posture: Establish the first high leg and its hand support before adding the second leg.
Bring the second leg high: Reinforce the clinch without forcing the knees beyond a comfortable hip angle.
Track both elbows: Do not assume that high legs alone have isolated an arm or completed Dead Orchard.
Keep knees close: Use hip position and connected leg pressure rather than pulling the feet against fixed knees.
Return to one-leg control: Lower the reinforcing leg while preserving the first shin connection if you need Mission Control again.
Open against a stack: Release and frame when the opponent compresses your upper back or you cannot comfortably maintain the clinch.

flashcards.question: Double Underhook Pass (bottom): Before release, what anchors your original high guard?
flashcards.answer: The first supported high leg is the foundation before any second-leg reinforcement.
flashcards.answer_line: The first high shin supported by its hand

plausible: The first high foot with the shin grip released
The second leg before the first shin is secured
trap: A low leg crossing with the shoulders already free

flashcards.question: Double Underhook Pass (bottom): Before both underhooks close, how can you recover a knee?
flashcards.answer: Once high guard opens, use shoulder frames and hip movement to bring a knee inside before both underhooks settle.
flashcards.answer_line: Frame the shoulders and shift the hips

plausible: Wait until both thighs are lifted before moving the hips
Turn one foot outward while the hips stay gathered
trap: Reach both hands behind the head with the hips still

flashcards.question: Double Underhook Pass (bottom): What would Dead Orchard require beyond arms beneath your thighs?
flashcards.answer: Track the actual shoulder-level enclosure. Arms under the thighs in a pass are not both arms trapped in Dead Orchard.
flashcards.answer_line: Both shoulders inside a high both-arm leg triangle

plausible: One shoulder inside a high triangle, with the other arm out
Both elbows below the knees in the hip-level clasp
trap: Both wrists held near the hips without high leg closure

flashcards.question: Double Underhook Pass (bottom): Your thighs are held; why avoid wrenching one knee sideways?
flashcards.answer: If the thighs are fixed, reset the drill rather than forcing a knee sideways against the grips.
flashcards.answer_line: The fixed grips can turn the knee into the moving joint

plausible: The knee turn releases the thigh clasp before force reaches the joint
The hip remains free to follow despite both thighs being controlled
trap: The ankle can pivot under a fixed thigh without loading the knee

flashcards.question: Double Underhook Pass (bottom): Before the clinch opens fully, how can you keep one high leg?
flashcards.answer: When comfortable and still available, retain the first high shin and hand while lowering the reinforcing leg.
flashcards.answer_line: Lower the second leg but retain the first shin connection

plausible: Release the shin grip while keeping the first foot high
Keep only the second leg and drop the original shin
trap: Lower the second leg and let the first knee drift away
